To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the E/M dip in PyrPC/DMPC vesicles arises from the long-range interaction between PyrPC molecules due to elastic deformation of the membrane matrix around bulky pyrenyl moieties, and that the depth of the dips decreases with increasing temperature, decreasing vesicle diameter, and increasing pressure.

the regular distribution of pyr-PC molecules into hexagonal super lattices is a self ordering phenomenon, and that the regular distribution is sensitive to the radius of curvature of the bilayer, the free volume of the membrane, and temperature.

the E/M dip in Pyr- PC/DMPC multilamellae is a consequence of regular distribution of Pyr-PC acyl chains into the hexagonal superlattices at critical PyrPC mole fractions, which are 33.3, 66.7, and 71.4% PyrPC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the exploration of physical principles underlying the regular distribution of lipid molecules.
the exploration of physical principles underlying regular distribution of pyrenelabeled acyl chains in lipid membranes.
the physical principles underlying the self-ordering of pyrene-lipids in binary PC mixtures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the physical principles underlying regular distribution of pyrenyl chains in the membrane are: (a) the long-range repulsion between pyrene-labeled chains due to elastic deformation of the lattice; (b) the long-range attractive interaction between pyrene-label chains; (c) the effect of curvature of the bilayer on the long-range interaction; (d) the effect of free volume in the bilayer on long-range interaction.
E/M dips are due to regular distribution of pyrenyl acyl chains at critical mole fractions of Pyr-PC.

the E/M dips in the plot versus Pyr-PC concentration arise from a self-ordered phenomenon of regular distribution of the bulky pyrene moieties into hexagonal superlattices.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the physical principles underlying lipid distribution are not well understood and require further study.
the regular distribution of lipids in a membrane can occur as a consequence of long-range repulsive forces between bulky lipids.
